transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My work physical is what kind of started this. The doctor there said my weight was too low and told me I should get checked out. I don’t really feel sick or anything—I feel lighter on my feet when I play basketball, and not as weighed down at the garage.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yeah… I guess I am, in a way. If the scale goes up even a pound, or my jeans feel a little tighter, I start thinking I’m getting soft. Like I’ll be slower at work moving around cars, or slower on the basketball court.
Do you think your weight is currently at a healthy level?

I mean, I know people are worried about it, but to me it doesn’t seem that unhealthy. I’m still going to work, getting stuff done around the house, and I can play basketball on the weekends. So I kind of feel like they’re making more of it than it is.
Do you think you would still be afraid of gaining weight if it didn't affect your performance at work or on the basketball court?

I think so, yeah. It’s not only the performance part. If I see the scale go up even a pound, or my jeans feel tighter, I just start thinking I’m getting soft. The work and basketball are where I notice it, but the number going up bothers me either way.
Do you think you would still feel good about your body if you gained a few pounds?

Probably not, no. If I gained a few pounds, I’d notice it right away—on the scale or if my jeans felt tighter—and I’d start thinking I was getting soft. Then I’d worry I’d be slower at work moving around cars or on the court.
Do you think you look too thin or just about right to yourself?

To me I look about right, honestly. I know other people think I’m too thin and they worry about it, but I feel like if I’m still getting to work, handling things at home, and playing ball on weekends, then it can’t be that bad. I think they may be making more of it than it is.
Do you think you look normal or underweight when you look in the mirror?

I guess I see myself as normal. I know people are worried and say I look underweight, but I don’t really see it that way. I’m still going to work, doing what I need to at home, and playing ball on weekends, so it feels like maybe they’re making too much of it.
Is there a specific weight or body shape that you think would be ideal for you?

I don’t have an exact number in mind, really. It’s more like… I know when it feels right. If the scale bumps up even a pound, or my jeans feel tighter, I start thinking I’m getting soft. Then I worry I won’t move as quick around the cars at work or up and down the court.
Do you think there's a certain body shape you're trying to maintain?

Yeah, I guess so. I’m trying to keep from getting, you know, soft. If the scale goes up even a pound or my jeans feel tighter, I start thinking I’ll be slower moving around cars at work or up and down the court.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is because of how you think you would look?

Yeah, partly, I guess. It’s not just how I look in the mirror, though. If the scale goes up even a pound or my jeans feel tighter, I start thinking I’m getting soft. Then I worry I’ll be slower moving around cars at work or running up and down the court.
Is your fear of gaining weight mostly because of how you think you would look to others?

Not mostly other people, no. It’s more what it means to me. If the scale goes up even a little, or my jeans feel tighter, I start thinking I’m getting soft. Then I worry I’ll be slower at work moving around the cars, or when I’m running up and down the court.
Do you think your weight or body shape is actually different from how you imagine it to be?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I know what I see and what I feel in my clothes, but I don’t know if that’s different from how it actually is. It’s hard for me to tell.
Do you think your body looks the way you imagine it to be?
I don’t really know. Sometimes it looks that way to me, but then I wonder if I’m just focusing on certain parts too much. It’s hard for me to be sure.
Do you think there's a difference between how you see your body and how it actually is?
I’m not sure, honestly. I can tell you how I see it, or how it feels to me, but I don’t really know what the “actual” version is. I might be off, but I can’t tell by how much.
Do you think your body image is accurate when you look in the mirror?
I’m not sure I can say it’s accurate. When I look in the mirror, I know what I think I’m seeing, but I don’t really know if that matches how I actually look. It’s hard for me to judge.
Is your fear of gaining weight more about how it would affect your appearance or how it would affect your ability to perform at work and in basketball?

It’s kind of both, but more tied together than separate. If the scale goes up even a pound, or my jeans feel tighter, I start thinking I’m getting soft. Then I worry I’ll be slower at work moving around cars, or slower up and down the court playing basketball.
When you think about gaining weight, what worries you more: how your body would look or how it would affect your performance at work and in basketball?

Probably more the performance part, but the way I look is tied into it. Like if the scale goes up even a pound, or my jeans feel tighter, I start thinking I’m getting soft. Then I worry I’ll be slower moving around cars at work or running up and down the court.
When you worry about gaining weight, is it more because you think you'll look unappealing or because you think you'll perform poorly at work or in basketball?

More because I think I’ll perform poorly, honestly. If the scale goes up even a pound, or my jeans feel tighter, I start thinking I’m getting soft, and then I worry I’ll be slower at work moving around cars or slower on the basketball court.
Do you think you would be afraid of gaining weight if you didn't care about how your body looks?

Yeah, I think I still would be. Even if I didn’t care how it looked, if the scale bumps up even a pound or my jeans feel tighter, I start thinking I’m getting soft. Then I worry I’ll be slower moving around cars at work or running up and down the court.
Would you say your fear of gaining weight is more about not wanting to lose athletic ability or more about not wanting to look a certain way?

More about not wanting to lose ability, I’d say. Like, if the scale goes up even a pound or my jeans feel tighter, I start thinking I’m getting soft, and then I worry I’ll be slower at work moving around cars or up and down the court.
